The Floyd Country Store, home of the Friday Night Jamboree, was constructed around 1910, and has been an important part of the community ever since. What is still most striking in the store though, is that as people walk through the door they cant help but smile.
The Jamboree starts every Friday at 6:30pm with an hour of bluegrass gospel music. At 7:30pm, dancers hit the floor, flatfooting and clogging to the music of regional Bluegrass or Old-Time bands. The music and dancing continues until at least 10:30pm, with an occasional two-step, square dance, or waltz thrown in for fun. If the crowd is willing, at 10:30pm we'll round up one of the jamming groups that can be found picking outside or upstairs in the store, and they will play for the crowd until around 11:30pm.

Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

Featuring:
• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

Presented by the Department of Art.

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

| Bennington        | 8/20/2011  | <div><b>You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. </b></div>  <div><b><br></b></div>  <style>@font-face {  font-family: "Times";  }@font-face {  font-family: "Cambria";  }p.MsoNormal, li.MsoNormal, div.MsoNormal { margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: "Times New Roman"; }a:link, span.MsoHyperlink { color: blue; text-decoration: underline; }a:visited, span.MsoHyperlinkFollowed { color: purple; text-decoration: underline; }div.Section1 { page: Section1; }</style>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This year will mark the 7<sup>th</sup>  year of this increasingly popular event.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic  River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research  and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association <a href="http://www.hoorwa.org/">http://www.hoorwa.org</a>. For the last six years  riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic  and just about every facet of the event. Two State Tour. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Each group  of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">. Commemorative ride jerseys are  available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr.  HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.   </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">THE 2011 ROUTES</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">: Named to honor the Ride’s founder  and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. | Bennington        | 8/20/2011  | <div><b>You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. </b></div>  <div><b><br></b></div>  <style>@font-face {  font-family: "Times";  }@font-face {  font-family: "Cambria";  }p.MsoNormal, li.MsoNormal, div.MsoNormal { margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: "Times New Roman"; }a:link, span.MsoHyperlink { color: blue; text-decoration: underline; }a:visited, span.MsoHyperlinkFollowed { color: purple; text-decoration: underline; }div.Section1 { page: Section1; }</style>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This year will mark the 7<sup>th</sup>  year of this increasingly popular event.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic  River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research  and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association <a href="http://www.hoorwa.org/">http://www.hoorwa.org</a>. For the last six years  riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic  and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new  routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have  seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great  theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great  getaway weekend. <i>Again this year the  venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington,  Vermont. </i><span> </span>Like last year, we  will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads  with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of  hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same  as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Each group  of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">. Commemorative ride jerseys are  available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr.  HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.   </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">THE 2011 ROUTES</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">: Named to honor the Ride’s founder  and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to  Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse  University crew team. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Lisa’s Three Challenge: </span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This<b> </b>75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This figure  eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the  4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on  this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route  includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of  stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain  you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and  its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well  as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of  descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic 50</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"></span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">It's just  that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York  countryside.<span>  </span>Last year was the  first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this  will be offered again, and again. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Two State Tour<br></span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Stay tuned for more route details;  there may be some changes.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The  Bridges and Monument  Loop</span></b></p>  <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument  and thru 3 covered bridges</span>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>RIDE DETAILS</b> </div>  <div><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Aid Station Items:</span> Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). The Jamboree starts every Friday at 6:30pm with an hour of bluegrass gospel music. At 7:30pm, dancers hit the floor, flatfooting and clogging to the music of regional Bluegrass or Old-Time bands. The music and dancing continues until at least 10:30pm, with an occasional two-step, square dance, or waltz thrown in for fun. Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. • Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

The Jamboree starts every Friday at 6:30pm with an hour of bluegrass gospel music. At 7:30pm, dancers hit the floor, flatfooting and clogging to the music of regional Bluegrass or Old-Time bands. The music and dancing continues until at least 10:30pm, with an occasional two-step, square dance, or waltz thrown in for fun. If the crowd is willing, at 10:30pm we'll round up one of the jamming groups that can be found picking outside or upstairs in the store, and they will play for the crowd until around 11:30pm.

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

Want to get up close and personal with one of America's most endangered mammals? Imagine finding yourself face to face and 15 feet from the endangered Red Wolf? An Animal Confidential Tour with VLM Curatorial Director George Mathews, Jr. will take you closer than your average visitor.
* Tour the otter and red wolf buildings
* Get closer to the raccoon enclosure and areas along the Outdoor Trail
* Find out the personal stories of our animals and why they are with us as well as what their lives were like before they came to the museum
* Find out what they eat, what activities we do to keep them healthy and observe special enrichment activities with the otter and raccoons

Ages 4+.

The Jamboree starts every Friday at 6:30pm with an hour of bluegrass gospel music. At 7:30pm, dancers hit the floor, flatfooting and clogging to the music of regional Bluegrass or Old-Time bands. The music and dancing continues until at least 10:30pm, with an occasional two-step, square dance, or waltz thrown in for fun. If the crowd is willing, at 10:30pm we'll round up one of the jamming groups that can be found picking outside or upstairs in the store, and they will play for the crowd until around 11:30pm.

Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine

• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

| Bennington        | 8/20/2011  | <div><b>You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. </b></div>  <div><b><br></b></div>  <style>@font-face {  font-family: "Times";  }@font-face {  font-family: "Cambria";  }p.MsoNormal, li.MsoNormal, div.MsoNormal { margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: "Times New Roman"; }a:link, span.MsoHyperlink { color: blue; text-decoration: underline; }a:visited, span.MsoHyperlinkFollowed { color: purple; text-decoration: underline; }div.Section1 { page: Section1; }</style>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This year will mark the 7<sup>th</sup>  year of this increasingly popular event.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic  River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research  and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association <a href="http://www.hoorwa.org/">http://www.hoorwa.org</a>. For the last six years  riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic  and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new  routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have  seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great  theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great  getaway weekend. <i>Again this year the  venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington,  Vermont. </i><span> </span>Like last year, we  will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads  with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of  hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same  as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Each group  of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">. Commemorative ride jerseys are  available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr.  HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.   </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">THE 2011 ROUTES</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">: Named to honor the Ride’s founder  and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to  Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse  University crew team. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Lisa’s Three Challenge: </span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This<b> </b>75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This figure  eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the  4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on  this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route  includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of  stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain  you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and  its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well  as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of  descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic 50</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"></span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">It's just  that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York  countryside.<span>  </span>Last year was the  first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this  will be offered again, and again. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Two State Tour<br></span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Stay tuned for more route details;  there may be some changes.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The  Bridges and Monument  Loop</span></b></p>  <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument  and thru 3 covered bridges</span>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>RIDE DETAILS</b> </div>  <div><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Aid Station Items:</span> Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations.  <span style="text-decoration: underline;">Post Ride Picnic:</span> Food, beverages, baked goods and more. </div>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>THE COST:</b> This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

Featuring:
• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

The ride starts from the Old Spokes Home bike shop in Burlington, VT at 4am. Please arrive by 3:30am to complete registration. Lighting & reflective equipment are optional on this ride for riders finishing before sunset. Please park on the street and not in the store's parking lot. 

Mote details about this and our other events can be found at the New England Randonneurs, Inc website.

Membership with New England Randonneurs (NER) is not required for this ride, but NER members save money. If you're a current RUSA member, you can become a NER member right now save $5 on this ride!

When you register you can optionally add an alternative phone number and alternative emergency contact number. These numbers are only used in a rare event of a ride cancellation or emergency. We will not disclose any rider-provided information to anyone other then event volunteers for the purposes of running events. (BikeReg has their own policies. To avoid paying the online registration fees, print and mail the 2011 NER registration form.

You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. 

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. 

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

Featuring:
• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

Love might make the world go ‘round, but Shakespeare never promises it will be an easy ride! While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

* Get closer to the raccoon enclosure and areas along the Outdoor Trail
* Find out the personal stories of our animals and why they are with us as well as what their lives were like before they came to the museum
* Find out what they eat, what activities we do to keep them healthy and observe special enrichment activities with the otter and raccoons
* Each animal species plays a role in the wild. This tour explains the cycle and how these animals are our special ambassadors for their species.

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

description: A hilarious whodunit in which the audience gets a chance to solve the crime.  There's a different murderer every night so the outcome is always a mystery.   Having performed over 10,000 times in Boston, Shear Madness has been acknowledged by the Guinness Book of World Records as the longest running play in American theater history.

The New York-New York Theatre presents Zumanity, Another Side of Cirque du Soleil. Beautiful performers entice the audience with a never-before-seen blend of fashion, art, music, dance, personality and sensuality.

The show begins the moment you walk through the door into Mystery Mansion Dinner Theatre.  Welcome to Greystone Manor.  You will be given a change of identity and whisked back to Hollywood in the roaring '20s.  C.D. Weasel, hollywood's colorful producer, has invited you to his mansion for a private screening of his motion picture masterpiece "Love's Foolish Parade."  You'll meet Edward Manly III, the dashing hero...or is he?  Then there's the sweet and innocent Clara Simpleton, who couldn't be as sweet as she seems.  There is a whole cast of intriguing characters who will entertain you and even serve you dinner.  Just remember:  one or more of them is a killer!

In this hilarious interactive comedy, the audience is part of the show.  As "invited guests" the audience begins the evening witnessing the holy nuptials. Following the ceremony, a rousing reception takes place at Vinnie Black's Coliseum.  Dancing, champagne toasts, a full pasta dinner and of course, a slice of the wedding cake are provided by the Nunzio and Vitale "families". Dazzling special effects highlight this tale of an American hero's struggle to tame heaven's own power.  This thrilling play for families culminates on a stormy night with the crack of thunder, a blinding flash of lightning and an experiment that changed the world!

Jesse, alienated from the pragmatism of his family and rural Virginia culture, draws and dreams of becoming something special. Leslie, the new girl from the city and the ultimate outsider, opens up a world of imagination, art and literature for him. Together they create Terabithia, a fantasy kingdom where they are safe from those who don't understand them. Their friendship grows as Jesse's world expands. When tragedy strikes, the strength gained in Terabithia lets Jesse move forward on his own, and lets him share the magic of his dreams.     Preteen/Young Adult Series.

Acclaimed as the debut of the year by one of the most exciting new writers in the country, Circle Mirror Transformation is the hilarious, moving new comedy about five citizens of a rural town who begin a community acting class, each with their own expectations, but soon learn more about each other and themselves than they bargained for. Circle Mirror Transformation has been hailed as one of the most insightful and original new plays of the year.

Marie is a pretty little girl with a pretty big heart. When the orphaned Marie is adopted by a regiment of the French soldiers, laughter erupts. The heartwarming story is filled with catchy tuneful music, two handfuls of tenor high C's and one energetic singing tomboy.
Choreography:  Jean Coralli & Jules Perrot  Music:  Adolphe Adam

Celebrate a revolutionary weekend! Our free, ever-popular reading of the Declaration of Independence features some of the most stirring words of political rhetoric ever written, spoken out loud by S&Co. actors and special guests from the community.

Ringing in the New Year with more laughs than should be legal, audiences will delight in the hilarious The Mystery of Irma Vep.  This zany romp through the mysterious and the sublime features two actors, eight roles (cue cross-dressing number), and wields a healthy mix of storytelling genres, from Hitchcock to Victorian melodrama to lurid, 19th century pulp fiction (or, in British parlance, 'penny dreadfuls'). This OBIE Award-winning, madcap escapade is sure to leave you breathless with laughter, while its expertly constructed story manages to both send-up and celebrate the traditional Gothic mystery.

The Declaration of Independence is preceded this year by Revolutionary Moments, a special collection of vignettes compiled by Tina Packer and featuring S&Co. actors. Part performance, part narration, part discussion, Revolutionary Moments highlights the influence of Shakespeare on some of history's most fascinating figures at key moments of decision. Not to be missed!

BODIES...The Exhibition, which showcases real full-bodies and organs, provides a detailed, three-dimensional vision of the human form rarely seen outside of an anatomy lab or a morgue. The Exhibition showcases 13 whole-body specimens and more than 260 organs and partial body specimens. These real human bodies have been meticulously dissected, preserved through an innovative process and respectfully presented, giving visitors the opportunity to view the beauty and complexity of their own organs and systems.

The 25,000-square-foot exhibit features numerous items from the Titanic, including luggage, the ship's whistles, floor tiles from the first-class smoking room, a window frame from the Verandah Cafe and an unopened bottle of champagne with a 1900 vintage. In addition, the exhibit features a piece of Titanic's hull, a full-scale re-creation of the Grand Staircase as well as a newly expanded outer Promenade Deck, complete with the frigid temperatures felt on that fateful April night.    These actual artifacts, recovered from two and one half miles below the surface of the North Atlantic, tell the story behind the legendary Titanic's short journey from construction and destruction to eventual recovery. Walk her decks, peer into her cabins and meet her passengers and crew.    Described as a floating palace, the incomparable Titanic was deemed "practically unsinkable" by the White Star Line and its builders. However, on a calm April night in 1912, the massive luxury liner struck an iceberg and slowly sank into the North Atlantic. Since then, many items from the wreckage have been recovered and added to Titanic: The Artifact Exhibition.     The personal artifacts on display offer haunting, emotional connections to the forever-altered lives of those on board the Titanic. Visitors even have a chance to walk through authentically re-created first- and third-class rooms, with furnishings by original manufacturers.

Experience a performance filled with the young energy, spirit and emotion of up-and-coming dancers from the Nancy Einhorn Milwaukee Ballet II program. These young artists come from every part of the U.S. to learn and participate in Milwaukee Ballet’s artistic repertoire rooted in classical ballet with a strong commitment to new and contemporary works.

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. * Get closer to the raccoon enclosure and areas along the Outdoor Trail
* Find out the personal stories of our animals and why they are with us as well as what their lives were like before they came to the museum

Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. Featuring:
• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

Presented by the Department of Art.

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

The ride starts from the Old Spokes Home bike shop in Burlington, VT at 4am. Please arrive by 3:30am to complete registration. Lighting & reflective equipment are optional on this ride for riders finishing before sunset. Please park on the street and not in the store's parking lot.

To avoid paying the online registration fees, print and mail the 2011 NER registration form.

You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. 

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

Featuring:
• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

Presented by the Department of Art.

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

| Bennington        | 8/20/2011  | <div><b>You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. </b></div>  <div><b><br></b></div>  <style>@font-face {  font-family: "Times";  }@font-face {  font-family: "Cambria";  }p.MsoNormal, li.MsoNormal, div.MsoNormal { margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: "Times New Roman"; }a:link, span.MsoHyperlink { color: blue; text-decoration: underline; }a:visited, span.MsoHyperlinkFollowed { color: purple; text-decoration: underline; }div.Section1 { page: Section1; }</style>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This year will mark the 7<sup>th</sup>  year of this increasingly popular event.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic  River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research  and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association <a href="http://www.hoorwa.org/">http://www.hoorwa.org</a>. For the last six years  riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic  and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new  routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have  seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great  theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great  getaway weekend. <i>Again this year the  venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington,  Vermont. </i><span> </span>Like last year, we  will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads  with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of  hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same  as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Each group  of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">. Commemorative ride jerseys are  available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr.  HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.   </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">THE 2011 ROUTES</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">: Named to honor the Ride’s founder  and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to  Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse  University crew team. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Lisa’s Three Challenge: </span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This<b> </b>75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This figure  eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the  4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on  this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route  includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of  stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain  you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and  its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well  as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of  descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic 50</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"></span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">It's just  that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York  countryside.<span>  </span>Last year was the  first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this  will be offered again, and again. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Two State Tour<br></span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Stay tuned for more route details;  there may be some changes.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The  Bridges and Monument  Loop</span></b></p>  <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument  and thru 3 covered bridges</span>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>RIDE DETAILS</b> </div>  <div><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Aid Station Items:</span> Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations.  <span style="text-decoration: underline;">Post Ride Picnic:</span> Food, beverages, baked goods and more. </div>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>THE COST:</b> This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

Love might make the world go ‘round, but Shakespeare never promises it will be an easy ride! Two young men travel to Milan, fall in love with the same woman, and so begins a tale of friendship and romance in one of the Bard’s earliest and most lyrical comedies. Our story continues with witty servants, outlaw kings, disguised maidens, and one very ill-behaved dog as the two gentlemen seek to the win the hand of the fairest woman in the land. While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

| Bennington        | 8/20/2011  | <div><b>You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. </b></div>  <div><b><br></b></div>  <style>@font-face {  font-family: "Times";  }@font-face {  font-family: "Cambria";  }p.MsoNormal, li.MsoNormal, div.MsoNormal { margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: "Times New Roman"; }a:link, span.MsoHyperlink { color: blue; text-decoration: underline; }a:visited, span.MsoHyperlinkFollowed { color: purple; text-decoration: underline; }div.Section1 { page: Section1; }</style>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This year will mark the 7<sup>th</sup>  year of this increasingly popular event.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic  River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research  and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association <a href="http://www.hoorwa.org/">http://www.hoorwa.org</a>. For the last six years  riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic  and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new  routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have  seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great  theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great  getaway weekend. <i>Again this year the  venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington,  Vermont. </i><span> </span>Like last year, we  will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads  with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of  hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same  as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Each group  of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">. Commemorative ride jerseys are  available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr.  HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.   </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">THE 2011 ROUTES</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">: Named to honor the Ride’s founder  and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to  Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse  University crew team. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Lisa’s Three Challenge: </span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This<b> </b>75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This figure  eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the  4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on  this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route  includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of  stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain  you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and  its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well  as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of  descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic 50</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"></span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">It's just  that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York  countryside.<span>  </span>Last year was the  first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this  will be offered again, and again. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Two State Tour<br></span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Stay tuned for more route details;  there may be some changes.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The  Bridges and Monument  Loop</span></b></p>  <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument  and thru 3 covered bridges</span>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>RIDE DETAILS</b> </div>  <div><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Aid Station Items:</span> Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. • Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. | Bennington        | 8/20/2011  | <div><b>You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. </b></div>  <div><b><br></b></div>  <style>@font-face {  font-family: "Times";  }@font-face {  font-family: "Cambria";  }p.MsoNormal, li.MsoNormal, div.MsoNormal { margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: "Times New Roman"; }a:link, span.MsoHyperlink { color: blue; text-decoration: underline; }a:visited, span.MsoHyperlinkFollowed { color: purple; text-decoration: underline; }div.Section1 { page: Section1; }</style>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This year will mark the 7<sup>th</sup>  year of this increasingly popular event.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic  River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research  and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association <a href="http://www.hoorwa.org/">http://www.hoorwa.org</a>. For the last six years  riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic  and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new  routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have  seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great  theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great  getaway weekend. <i>Again this year the  venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington,  Vermont. </i><span> </span>Like last year, we  will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads  with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of  hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). Two State Tour. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Each group  of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">.
